record.experiment_description:
Objectives:

The objectives of this experiment were 1) to examine the time course of myosin heavy chain expression and the development of adult fiber types in hindlimb muscles which have been exposed to microgravity during embryonic development 2) to determine if microgravity exposure during embryogenesis influences postnatal development of the neuromuscular system evaluated by morphological and biochemical studies, and 3) to determine if the embryonic system requires gravity as an orienting force in order to establish normal differentiation of muscle fiber types.

Approach:

Protein expression was quantified using SDS PAGE gel-electrophoresis and immunohistochemistry. Monoclonal antibodies specific for the myosin heavy chain (MHC) (embryonic, neonatal, slow, fast IIa, IIb, and IIx) were used to examine MHC expression in individual muscle fibers. Tissue was frozen fresh without fixative. The expression of mRNA was examined using in situ histochemistry and Northern blots. Radiolabeled riboprobes specific for various muscle specific genes were made and used to detect mRNA expression in post-fixed muscle cross-sections. Riboprobes for the MHC (embryonic, neonatal, slow, IIa,IIb, and IIx) fast and slow sarcoplasmic reticulum ATPase, troponin C, myogenic regulatory factors (myogenin and myoD) and growth factors (FGF and IGF) were used. Electron microscopy was used to determine the number of primary and secondary fibers in the fetal neonatal hindlimbs.

Results:

In soleus and medial gastrocnemius muscles from the dams, on differences were found between flight and control animals in mean fiber area or myosin heavy chain expression.
